Class Searchables

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.jpa.search.Searchables
public final class Searchables extends Object
Utility class for building JPA Criteria API predicates based on fields marked with Searchable.

This utility automatically generates case-insensitive LIKE predicates for all String fields or methods annotated with @Searchable: every word of the search term must appear in at least one of them. It handles SQL wildcard escaping and provides null-safe operation.

Key Features

  • Annotation-Driven: Automatically discovers @Searchable fields
  • Case-Insensitive: All searches use lowercase comparison
  • Wildcard Escaping: Automatically escapes %, _, and \
  • Word by Word: The term is split on whitespace; a row matches when every word appears in at least one searchable field, in any order (at most 10 words are used)
  • Null-Safe: Returns all results when search term is null or blank
  • Type-Safe: Only processes String fields

Usage Examples

With SearchableRepository (Recommended)

@Repository
public interface PersonRepository extends SearchableRepository<Person, UUID> {
    // search() method is inherited
}

@Service
public class PersonService {

    private static final Paginator PAGINATOR = Paginator.of(Person.class, PersonSort.class);

    @Autowired
    private PersonRepository personRepository;

    public PageDto<PersonDto> search(String query, PageSpec pageSpec) {
        return PAGINATOR.paginate(pageSpec,
                pageable -> personRepository.search(query, pageable),
                PersonDto::fromEntity);
    }
}

Manual Usage with JpaSpecificationExecutor

@Repository
public interface PersonRepository extends JpaRepository<Person, UUID>, JpaSpecificationExecutor<Person> {
}

@Service
public class PersonService {

    @Autowired
    private PersonRepository personRepository;

    public Page<Person> search(String query, Pageable pageable) {
        Specification<Person> spec = (root, criteriaQuery, criteriaBuilder) ->
            Searchables.createSearchPredicate(query, root, criteriaBuilder);

        return personRepository.findAll(spec, pageable);
    }
}

Combining with Other Specifications

@Service
public class PersonService {

    @Autowired
    private PersonRepository personRepository;

    public Page<Person> searchActive(String query, Pageable pageable) {
        Specification<Person> searchSpec = (root, criteriaQuery, criteriaBuilder) ->
            Searchables.createSearchPredicate(query, root, criteriaBuilder);

        Specification<Person> activeSpec = (root, criteriaQuery, criteriaBuilder) ->
            criteriaBuilder.isTrue(root.get("active"));

        // Combine specifications: search AND active
        Specification<Person> combined = searchSpec.and(activeSpec);

        return personRepository.findAll(combined, pageable);
    }
}

Example Entity

@Entity
public class Person extends BaseEntity {

    @Searchable
    private String firstName;

    @Searchable
    private String lastName;

    @Searchable
    private String email;

    private String internalNotes;  // NOT searchable

    // When searching for "john", will match:
    // - firstName LIKE '%john%' OR
    // - lastName LIKE '%john%' OR
    // - email LIKE '%john%'
}

Search Behavior

Wildcard Escaping

Special SQL wildcard characters are automatically escaped:

// User searches for: "100%"
// Automatically escaped to: "100\%"
// SQL LIKE pattern becomes: "%100\\%%"

// User searches for: "test_value"
// Automatically escaped to: "test\_value"
// SQL LIKE pattern becomes: "%test\\_value%"

Null and Blank Handling

// Null search term - returns ALL results
Predicate predicate = Searchables.createSearchPredicate(null, root, builder);
// Result: builder.conjunction() (always true)

// Blank search term - returns ALL results
Predicate predicate = Searchables.createSearchPredicate("   ", root, builder);
// Result: builder.conjunction() (always true)

// Empty search term - returns ALL results
Predicate predicate = Searchables.createSearchPredicate("", root, builder);
// Result: builder.conjunction() (always true)

No Searchable Fields

// If entity has no @Searchable fields
Predicate predicate = Searchables.createSearchPredicate("query", root, builder);
// Result: builder.conjunction() (always true, returns all results)

Performance Considerations

  • Database Indexes: LIKE queries with leading wildcards (%term%) cannot use indexes efficiently
  • Query Size: The predicate has one LIKE per word per @Searchable field
  • Full-Text Search: For large text fields or complex search requirements, consider database-specific full-text search
  • Pagination: Always use pagination to limit result sets

Limitations

  • Only supports String fields/methods
  • Does not search across entity relationships
  • Uses simple LIKE queries (not full-text search)
  • Leading wildcard (%term) prevents index usage

  • Method Details

    • createSearchPredicate

      public static jakarta.persistence.criteria.Predicate createSearchPredicate(String searchTerm, jakarta.persistence.criteria.Root<?> root, jakarta.persistence.criteria.CriteriaBuilder builder)
      Creates a JPA Criteria API predicate that searches all @Searchable String fields.

      The search term is split on whitespace into words (lowercased, duplicates dropped, at most 10). A row matches when every word appears, case-insensitively, in at least one searchable field, so "john smith" finds a row with firstName = "John" and lastName = "Smith", in either order. SQL wildcards in the words are escaped.

      Behavior:

      • If searchTerm is null or blank → returns builder.conjunction() (all results)
      • If no @Searchable fields exist → returns builder.conjunction() (all results)
      • Otherwise → an AND, over the words, of an OR over the searchable fields

      Search Pattern:

      // Input: "john smith"
// SQL: WHERE (LOWER(firstName) LIKE '%john%' ESCAPE '\' OR LOWER(lastName) LIKE '%john%' ESCAPE '\')
//        AND (LOWER(firstName) LIKE '%smith%' ESCAPE '\' OR LOWER(lastName) LIKE '%smith%' ESCAPE '\')
      Parameters:
      searchTerm - the search term to match (case-insensitive, wildcards escaped), may be null or blank
      root - the query root representing the entity, must not be null
      builder - the criteria builder for constructing predicates, must not be null
      Returns:
      a predicate matching every word of the search term across the searchable fields, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if root or builder is null
